candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes a filariform larva within a medium-caliber artery of the choroid and disseminated infection in an immunocompromised patient (hyper-IgE syndrome on prednisone, alcohol use disorder) in the rural southeastern US — a classic hyperinfection syndrome setting for Strongyloides stercoralis. The larval morphology (filariform, coiled in an artery) and systemic dissemination pattern are characteristic of Strongyloides, not Toxocara. While both can produce eosinophil-rich choroidal infiltrates, Toxocara does not cause the described disseminated multi-organ involvement or filariform larvae in vascular structures. The candidate correctly identifies ocular eosinophilic choroiditis but assigns an incompatible causative organism and lacks the disseminated systemic component.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Ocular toxocariasis vs. disseminated Strongyloides stercoralis with ocular choroiditis

case_quality_flags: Autopsy finding of filariform larva in choroidal artery is pathognomonic for Strongyloides hyperinfection, clearly distinguishing it from Toxocara
Concurrent disseminated aspergillosis and candidiasis reflect profound immunosuppression consistent with Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome
